hypothesis: Quantum kernel OC-SVM (Kyriienko & Magnusson) beats classical anomaly detectors on our exact same source dataset
architecture: OneClassSVM(kernel=quantum fidelity, CLT and linear topology) at 4/6 qubits, trained on legitimate-only rows
result: 4q: quantum 0.8628/0.8708 < classical_rbf 0.8789 < isolation_forest 0.9145. 6q: quantum(linear) 0.9390 > classical_rbf 0.9329 > isolation_forest 0.9305 (a positive point estimate)
reason_rejected: At 6q the point estimate favors the quantum kernel, but a 2000-resample paired bootstrap gives 95% CIs of [-0.0236,+0.0384] (vs RBF) and [-0.0184,+0.0389] (vs Isolation Forest) -- both cross zero, so not statistically distinguishable from noise on n=100 validation rows, single seed.
what_was_learned: This is the first result anywhere in this project's quantum research where a quantum method's raw point estimate beat every classical alternative on a real evaluation -- worth flagging honestly as 'promising but unverified' per the project's own promotion rules, not dismissed, but also not claimed as a finding until multi-seed + larger-N confirmation exists. Also: at 4 qubits the quantum kernel underperformed both classical baselines, so the qubit-count dependence seen in the earlier CLT-vs-random-sparse study repeats here.

hypothesis: Local-sum observable (Cerezo et al. locality argument) meaningfully improves QNN mean PR-AUC
architecture: EstimatorQNN with observable = (1/n)*sum_i Z_i vs the implicit global Z^n default, 5 seeds, 4 qubits, CLT topology
reason_rejected: local_sum mean PR-AUC 0.7947 (std 0.0260) vs global mean 0.7737 (std 0.0609); local_single (Z on one qubit only) was worse at 0.7178 (std 0.0596)
what_was_learned: The mean improvement (+0.0210) is well within one seed-standard-deviation of the current default (0.0609), so it cannot yet be called an established accuracy improvement from 5 seeds alone -- would need a paired bootstrap across matched seeds or many more seeds to confirm.
column7: The variance reduction is the more defensible partial finding: local_sum's seed-to-seed std (0.0260) is roughly 2.3x smaller than the global observable's (0.0609), consistent with Cerezo et al.'s prediction that local cost functions are more trainable (less prone to gradient concentration/barren-plateau-like behavior) than global ones, even at circuit sizes far smaller than the paper's own 100-qubit demonstration. This is a training-stability finding, not a confirmed accuracy win, and is reported as such.

hypothesis: Full Kyriienko-style scaling sweep up to 20 qubits reproducing their reported 15pp AP gap
reason_rejected: Their reported effect only emerges at >10 qubits on their larger controlled subsample; our locked controlled subset caps at 4/6/8 qubits per this project's own qubit-scaling policy (more qubits requires justification from smaller-scale results first, per the qubit-scaling caution already established in layer1_context.md Section 13), and even 6 qubits already took ~140-150s per kernel fit -- 8+ qubits would scale further given O(n_nominal^2) fidelity evaluation cost.
what_was_learned: Not pursued this round given the 4q/6q result was already mixed (worse at 4q, promising-but-unverified at 6q) -- scaling to more qubits without first confirming the 6q result across seeds would be premature.
